html:
On 11 October 1865 hundreds of poor Black farmers, led by the Baptist deacon Paul Bogle, marched on the courthouse at Morant Bay in Jamaica. Militia fired, and the crowd burned the building and killed officials.

Thirty years after emancipation, freed people still had little land, low wages and no say in government. Governor Edward Eyre answered with martial law. Troops killed hundreds, flogged hundreds more and burned a thousand homes. Bogle and the politician George William Gordon were hanged.

The brutality caused uproar in Britain and Eyre was recalled. Jamaica's old planter assembly gave up its powers, and the island became a crown colony ruled from London. Bogle and Gordon are now National Heroes.
